A grade-band value schedule (threshold-economics loss)

Source: R/loss-grade-band.R
grade_band_value.Rd

Builds a step value schedule: a payoff that is constant within a quality band and jumps at each breakpoint. This is the canonical shape of a quality-graded payoff – a grain price that steps up as protein clears 10.5%, 11.5%, and 13%, say – where the value of an outcome depends on which band it falls in, not on its exact magnitude. The returned object is a vectorised function from a quality outcome to its band payoff, classed so it carries the schedule for inspection and prints as a readable band table.

Usage

grade_band_value(breaks, values, right = FALSE, labels = NULL)

Arguments

breaks

A strictly increasing numeric vector of band edges (e.g. the protein thresholds c(10.5, 11.5, 13)).

values

A numeric vector of band payoffs, of length length(breaks) + 1, ordered from the lowest band to the highest.

right

Logical; when FALSE (default) bands are [lower, upper) so an outcome on a break clears into the higher band; when TRUE bands are (lower, upper].

[lower, upper)so an outcome on a break clears into the higher band; whenTRUEbands are(lower, upper]: R:lower,%20upper)%60%20so%20an%0Aoutcome%20on%20a%20break%20clears%20into%20the%20higher%20band;%20when%20%60TRUE%60%20bands%20are%0A%60(lower,%20upper

labels

Optional character labels for the bands, of length length(values); defaults to formatted interval strings.

Value

A function of one numeric argument returning the band payoff for each element, with class grade_band_value and the schedule stored as attributes (breaks, values, labels, right).

Details

breaks are the band edges, strictly increasing. values are the payoffs, one per band: the first applies below breaks[1], the last applies at or above breaks[length(breaks)], and each interior element applies between a consecutive pair of breaks. With right = FALSE (the default) each band is the half-open interval [lower, upper), so an outcome exactly on a break clears into the higher band – the convention a delivery standard uses when it pays the better grade at the threshold.

See also

grade_band_utility() to turn the schedule into a decide() utility; decide() for the engine that consumes it.

Other loss: grade_band_utility()

Examples

# An APW-style protein payoff: $/t steps up as protein clears each band.
v <- grade_band_value(breaks = c(10.5, 11.5, 13),
                      values = c(300, 330, 360, 400))
v(c(9.0, 11.0, 11.5, 14.0))
#> [1] 300 330 360 400
v
#> <grade_band_value> 4 bands
#>          band value
#>  [-Inf, 10.5)   300
#>  [10.5, 11.5)   330
#>    [11.5, 13)   360
#>     [13, Inf)   400
